counterfactual_missing_items: Positive bone marrow involvement would shift from primary CNS lymphoma to secondary CNS lymphoma; bone marrow is negative for lymphoma cells.
Positive MYC rearrangement would imply a high-grade/double-hit B-cell process; FISH shows no MYC abnormalities.
EBV/EBER positivity would point toward an EBV-driven lymphoproliferative process; the biopsy is EBV/EBER−.

response.rationale: C1 is the more complete candidate because it adds the B-cell phenotypic subtype supported by CD19+, CD20+, BCL6+, and MUM-1+ on biopsy. R3 expresses the same core diagnosis without the subtype and is the only near competitor. R5, R7, and R4 are unsupported by definitive pathology and contradicted by CSF lymphoma cells and the B-cell immunophenotype.

rejected.why: The MRI white-matter pattern is nonspecific, and the brain biopsy B-cell immunophenotype plus CSF lymphoma cells are incompatible with PML.
CSF lymphoma positivity and the B-cell IHC profile do not fit a primary demyelinating disease such as multiple sclerosis.
The biopsied lesion is B-lineage lymphoma, not glioma; absence of contrast enhancement alone does not support glioblastoma.
